prompt:
Production Unity sprite animation sheet for Tank. Reference defines exact enemy identity, silhouette and perspective. Create redrawn articulated action frames of this same creature. Matte dark rock-brown armor, pale gray-white sinew, subtle amber slit eyes, clean painterly pre-rendered 3D style. Fixed elevated 45deg game view, soft upper-left lighting. Massive squat broad quadruped with thick layered irregular rock-brown armor boulders, huge pale gray sinewy muscular FOUR legs, blunt low armored head and amber eye slit, broad heavy body. Preserve the reference's wide tank silhouette. No green/red/purple dorsal sacs, no extra limbs or spikes.
EVERY frame faces: LEFT profile facing screen left, nose at left edge of body and tail at right; keep this direction in EVERY pose. No camera or body angle changes during abilities/death. 
Grid EXACTLY FOUR columns and 6 rows; 24 complete separate bodies. PORTRAIT canvas width-to-height 4:6. Each creature fits middle 60% of its cell; generous transparent gutters so no neighboring toes/armor touch. Same body scale and ground anchor throughout. Rows1-2: EIGHT sequential heavy WALK frames, four legs take distinct weight-bearing steps, alternating diagonal pairs, subtle weight shift, stable armor. Row3: FOUR IDLE breathing poses, planted feet. Row4: FOUR shockwave WINDUP frames: hind legs brace, front limbs and chest gradually lift a little, ready to pound ground, preserve full anatomy. Row5: FOUR SLAM/RECOVERY frames: FIRST frame both front feet firmly strike ground with head lowered, then armored body absorbs impact, shoulders recoil and settles; no drawn shockwave, dust, debris or ground. Row6: FOUR DEATH frames, heavy legs progressively lose support, armor settles flat, head rests, amber eye darkens.
Draw genuine distinct joint motion; do not copy identical stills or merely rotate/scale. Maintain anatomy and plate layout. Full transparent alpha0 background, including between legs. No opaque brown backdrop, no ground/shadow, text, labels, grid, particles or projectiles.
